question: With P3 representation, capacity, initialisation and training schedule held fixed, does vanilla SAM training improve generalisation over the same-round AdamW control?

scope.type: training-method exploration, not an architecture contribution and not a sharpness causal diagnosis
arms: S:P3-SAM (vanilla global L2 SAM, base optimizer AdamW)
scope.official_test_status: historically exposed benchmark; described, not a new blind test

data.target_transform: none (no clipping, reweighting or extra supervision)
data.normalization: frozen P3 train-only global-33 mean/scale (analysis/norm.json of zinc_arch_discovery_v1)
data.pretraining: frozen P3 train-only masked SSL encoders, no labels

model.builder: ad2_models.build_model('P3N', norm, seed=0) -> ad_models.P3Encoders + Null grouping + composer + reader

ssl.composer_reader_init: fresh random init from torch.manual_seed(0), shared by both arms

forbidden_inits: L or DBT or A_joint_BF checkpoints

optimizer.name: adamw
optimizer.grad_clip_scope: C: its update gradient; S: second-pass (perturbed) gradient only
optimizer.schedule: 500 outer updates linear warmup, then per-step cosine over the fixed 47,400-update horizon

schedule.selection: min valid MAE, strict <, ties keep the earlier epoch

sam.type: vanilla global L2 SAM (non-adaptive, all optimised parameters incl. biases)
sam.epsilon: rho * g1_p / (||g1||_2 + 1e-12), g1 raw and unclipped

reference.note: reference rows are reused, not retrained; the same-round C vs S contrast is the main table

groups.unseen: existing audited content-key aligned radius-2 signature flag
groups.usage: post-hoc description only; no new thresholds, no gating

time_plan.formal_reset: rebuild from the same initial state_dict and reseed the row-order RNG
time_plan.gpu_hours_note: SAM does two forward/backward per outer update; the comparison is at equal outer updates, not equal compute
